title: Brown's work witnessed by top government and military figures

tellings.quote: One in which Townsen Brown isn't easily dismissed as an amateur quack. In fact, his work was witnessed by the highest levels of government and military.

plain: The work of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, which Michels ties to antigravity propulsion, was witnessed at the highest levels of the US government and military, Michels says. He draws on a biography of Brown by the writer Paul Schatzkin and names figures linked to the story, among them Curtis Lame, the physicist Edward Teller, the jet maker Bill Lear and a man named Agnew Bahnson. Michels makes the point to argue that Brown can't simply be written off as an amateur crank.
